entry.title: USN-7626-3: Git regression
entry.summary:
USN-7626-1 fixed vulnerabilities in Git. The updates for CVE-2025-27613 and CVE-2025-46835 caused gitk and git-gui to not work properly on Ubuntu 16.04 LTS, Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, and were disabled in USN-7626-2. The problematic updates for the aforementioned CVEs have now been corrected and reinstated in this update.
We apologize for the inconvenience.
Original advisory details:
Avi Halachmi discovered that Git incorrectly managed file modification constraints with Gitk. An attacker could possibly use this issue to create or write to arbitrary files on the system. (CVE-2025-27613)
Avi Halachmi discovered that Git incorrectly handled arguments when invoking the Gitk utility. If a user were tricked into cloning a malicious Git repository, an attacker could possibly use this issue to run arbitrary commands. This issue only affected Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.10, and Ubuntu 25.04. (CVE-2025-27614)
Johannes Sixt discovered that Git incorrectly managed file modification constraints with Git GUI. If a user were tricked into editing a file in a malicious Git repository, an attacker could possibly use this issue to create or write to arbitrary files on the system. (CVE-2025-46835)
David Leadbeater discovered that Git incorrectly stripped CRLF characters when editing configuration files. An attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2025-48384)
David Leadbeater discovered that Git incorrectly handled verification when fetching remote Git repositories. An attacker could possibly use this issue to perform protocol injection, leading to arbitrary code execution. This issue only affected Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.10, and Ubuntu 25.04. (CVE-2025-48385)
David Leadbeater discovered that Git incorrectly handled memory with the wincred credential helper. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. (CVE-2025-48386)

entry.title: How to use custom playbooks in Dynasty in College Football 26
entry.summary:
College Football 26 takes sports sims to the next level, bringing back another year of scholastic football excellence on the gridiron.
Before taking and doling out hits on the field, you have to make some hits in the study room when it comes to your playbook for both offense and defense. You can use any existing playbook from real world coaches in the game, or you can put in the work and make your own, piece by piece.
Custom Playbooks are back in CFB 26, and here's how to use yours in Dynasty mode.
College Football 26 Dynasty mode - Custom Playbooks
Screenshot by Destructoid
First, make a custom playbook. To do this, navigate to the Create & Share tab at the main menu (L1/R1, LB/RB on the controller), then select Custom Playbooks. Here you can select plays from preset playbooks and real-life coach playbooks to make your own.
You can tweak and edit existing playbooks to remove plays you don't want, or you can start from scratch and make your own full of genius tricks, options, blitzes, and wild coverages to keep your opponents guessing in every mode.
Now, once in Dynasty mode, you can select your custom playbooks for each individual game. When you're ready to take the field for gameday, at the team select menu, select your squad and then Team Settings. On the next screen, you can swap your Offense and Defense playbooks and find any custom ones you've made, like my "CUSTOM335" defense playbook in the image below.
Screenshot by Destructoid
Like CFB 25, you won't be able to add custom playbooks to your Coach page under the Schemes & Playbook section. You will have to select your custom playbooks at the start of each game in Dynastry for them to take effect once the game kicks off.

entry.title: USN-7626-2: Git regression
entry.summary:
USN-7626-1 fixed vulnerabilities in Git. The update introduced a regression in gitk and git-gui. This update reverts the corresponding fixes for CVE-2025-27613 and CVE-2025-46835 pending further investigation.
We apologize for the inconvenience.
Original advisory details:
Avi Halachmi discovered that Git incorrectly managed file modification constraints with Gitk. An attacker could possibly use this issue to create or write to arbitrary files on the system. (CVE-2025-27613)
Avi Halachmi discovered that Git incorrectly handled arguments when invoking the Gitk utility. If a user were tricked into cloning a malicious Git repository, an attacker could possibly use this issue to run arbitrary commands. This issue only affected Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.10, and Ubuntu 25.04. (CVE-2025-27614)
Johannes Sixt discovered that Git incorrectly managed file modification constraints with Git GUI. If a user were tricked into editing a file in a malicious Git repository, an attacker could possibly use this issue to create or write to arbitrary files on the system. (CVE-2025-46835)
David Leadbeater discovered that Git incorrectly stripped CRLF characters when editing configuration files. An attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2025-48384)
David Leadbeater discovered that Git incorrectly handled verification when fetching remote Git repositories. An attacker could possibly use this issue to perform protocol injection, leading to arbitrary code execution. This issue only affected Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.10, and Ubuntu 25.04. (CVE-2025-48385)
David Leadbeater discovered that Git incorrectly handled memory with the wincred credential helper. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service. (CVE-2025-48386)
